## Purpose and Repository Shape
This is a curated Kubernetes manifest repository, not a single deployable application. Its entry points are category/example README files and Kubernetes resource manifests applied by users. Active examples are organized around AI, web workloads, databases, and a platform app; historical material is isolated under `_archived/`.

## AI Model Serving
TensorFlow serving is expressed as a deployment exposed through a Service and optional Ingress, with persistent model storage defined separately:
- `AI/model-serving-tensorflow/deployment.yaml`
- `AI/model-serving-tensorflow/service.yaml`
- `AI/model-serving-tensorflow/pv.yaml`

The vLLM example similarly deploys GPU-backed inference behind an in-cluster Service:
- `AI/vllm-deployment/vllm-deployment.yaml`
- `AI/vllm-deployment/vllm-service.yaml`

## GPU Autoscaling and Observability Boundary
vLLM’s optional HPA stack connects inference workload metrics to Kubernetes scaling. DCGM exporter Services expose GPU metrics; ServiceMonitors and Prometheus rules/adapter make those metrics consumable by HPAs:
- `AI/vllm-deployment/hpa/gpu-horizontal-pod-autoscaler.yaml`
- `AI/vllm-deployment/hpa/prometheus-adapter.yaml`
- `AI/vllm-deployment/hpa/vllm-service-monitor.yaml`

This boundary requires Prometheus-compatible monitoring and, depending on the manifest variant, generic Kubernetes or GKE-specific GPU metric discovery.

## Web Application Patterns
The maintained guestbook examples demonstrate multi-tier request/data flows: a frontend Service routes to frontend pods, which use Redis master/replica services for state. Modern manifests are separated by tier:
- `web/guestbook/frontend-deployment.yaml`
- `web/guestbook/redis-master-deployment.yaml`
- `web/guestbook/redis-replica-deployment.yaml`

An alternate Go implementation packages application source plus separate Redis controllers/services:
- `web/guestbook-go/main.go`
- `web/guestbook-go/guestbook-controller.yaml`
- `web/guestbook-go/redis-master-controller.yaml`

A minimal NGINX platform workload is deployment-and-service only:
- `nginx-platform-app/deployment.yml`
- `nginx-platform-app/service.yml`

## Stateful Database Patterns
Cassandra is the principal active stateful example. A StatefulSet and Service establish cluster identity/discovery, while a custom image and seed-provider integration support Kubernetes-aware membership:
- `databases/cassandra/cassandra-statefulset.yaml`
- `databases/cassandra/cassandra-service.yaml`
- `databases/cassandra/java/src/main/java/io/k8s/cassandra/KubernetesSeedProvider.java`

Its runtime spans Cassandra/JVM plus Go/Java integration artifacts and image bootstrap scripts. MySQL demonstrates persistent-disk-backed database deployment:
- `databases/mysql-cinder-pd/mysql.yaml`
- `databases/mysql-cinder-pd/mysql-service.yaml`

## Infrastructure and Control Model
Kubernetes is the runtime and reconciliation engine throughout: Deployments/Controllers manage stateless pods, StatefulSets manage stable database members, Services provide discovery/load balancing, and PV/PVC manifests bind workloads to cluster storage. Ingress is an external HTTP entry boundary where supplied. GPU examples additionally depend on GPU-capable nodes, DCGM metrics, and Prometheus/HPA infrastructure.

## Archived Compatibility Corpus
`_archived/` contains older or retired examples spanning storage, databases, monitoring, and workload controllers. It is intentionally separated from current examples and should not be treated as the primary architecture surface:
- `_archived/storage/`
- `_archived/volumes/`
- `_archived/cloud-controller-manager/`
